pll2d15c6-d1e3519.summary: Reports others who think things were not made over intervals but came forth formed at once.
claims: Another view: all things were formed at once.

pll2d15c6-d1e3522.summary: Cites Augustine's arguments that the four elements existed formed as now from the beginning and heaven was adorned with stars, while some things were made materially, not formally, then later distinguished, like plants, trees, and perhaps animals. So all was made at the beginning of time, some formally, the major parts of the world, some only materially.
claims: The major parts were made formed at once.
Other things were made materially and formed later.

pll2d15c6-d1e3542.summary: Explains their view that Moses, speaking to a rude and carnal people, adapted his speech, describing God like a man who completes works over time, though God made them simultaneously.
claims: Moses accommodated his account to a simple people.

pll2d15c6-d1e3546.summary: Cites Augustine: Moses relates God's works separately because what God could do at once could not be said at once by a man.
claims: Speech is successive though God's act was simultaneous.

pll2d15c6-d1e3561.summary: Further Augustine: Scripture could divide by times of speaking what God did not divide by times of working.
claims: Scripture divides in speech what God did at once.

pll2d15c6-d1e3573.summary: Concludes that those following these authorities, holding that the elements and luminaries had formed being at once, call the six days six kinds of things or distinctions made at once, partly formally, partly causally.
claims: The six days are six kinds made at once.

pl-l2d15c6.summary: Presents the other view: things were not made over intervals but formed simultaneously. Augustine argues that the four elements existed formed from the beginning and heaven was adorned with stars, while some things (plants, trees, perhaps animals) were made materially and later formed. Moses, speaking to a rude people, described God's simultaneous work as successive, since what God could do at once could not be said at once; the six days are six kinds of things made together, partly formally, partly causally.
claims: Some hold all things were made simultaneously.
Augustine holds the elements and stars were formed from the start, other things made materially and formed later.
Moses described simultaneous creation successively for a rude people.
On this view the six days are six kinds of things made at once, partly formally, partly causally.
